items.item: Approve 4K program agreements with community partners for 2027-2028
items.why: The board will vote to continue and expand formal partnerships between the district's preschool program and sites including Wausau Child Care, Mountain View Montessori, Newman Catholic Schools, and two previously partnered organizations.

items.item: Review and vote on updated district policies (35 policies total)
items.why: The board will consider updates to 35 policies covering curriculum, student discipline, food services, transportation, surveillance, and other operations.

items.item: Hear staff turnover and retention report across all employee groups
items.why: Tabatha Gundrum will present data on employee turnover by job category and discuss planned responses to address retention challenges.

items.item: Review 2026-2027 student enrollment and demographic data
items.why: Director of Technology Ralph Williams will present enrollment numbers and demographic information for the upcoming school year.

items.item: Receive update on referendum budget spending
items.why: Dr. Elizabeth Channel will update the board on how money from the district's referendum is being spent.

items.item: Review changes to 6th through 12th grade social studies curriculum
items.why: The board will consider an adjusted curriculum scope and sequence for secondary social studies and hear about the adjustment process and timeline.

preview.overview: The Wausau School Board will approve agreements for its preschool program partners and vote on updated district policies. The board will also hear updates on staff turnover, student enrollment, and curriculum changes.

items.item: 2027 budgets for five housing programs
items.why: The board is scheduled to vote on separate budgets for the Housing Choice Voucher Program, Public Housing Program, Riverview Terrace, Riverview Towers, Fulton Street, and 8th Avenue.

items.item: Repositioning scattered public housing to voucher-based model
items.why: The board will hear a presentation on comprehensive repositioning options and vote on Resolution #26-012 to convert scattered-sites public housing to project-based vouchers.

items.item: Riverview Towers façade repair bids
items.why: The board is scheduled to review and act on bids received for masonry and concrete façade repairs at Riverview Towers.

items.item: Capital needs assessment for scattered-sites properties
items.why: The board will consider a request for proposals for a capital needs assessment of scattered-sites public housing properties.

items.item: Sub-recipient agreement for 405 S 8th Avenue
items.why: The board will discuss and act on a rental property agreement between the city and the authority for 405 S 8th Avenue.

items.item: Outside counsel for Section 18 repositioning
items.why: The board will address legal procurement needs for Section 18 repositioning and tax credit close-out work.

preview.overview: The Community Development Authority is scheduled to vote on 2027 budgets for five housing programs and consider a major plan to convert scattered public housing sites to voucher-based housing.

items.item: 3rd Quarter Fire Department Operations Report
items.why: The Fire Department will present its quarterly operations update to the commission.

items.item: Police Department General Operations Update
items.why: The Police Department will provide general updates on its operations.

items.item: Interview five police officer candidates and one fire lieutenant promotion candidate
items.why: The commission will meet in closed session to interview candidates for a police officer position and a fire lieutenant promotion.

items.item: Reconsideration request of citizen complaint dismissal
items.why: The commission will consider in closed session a request to reconsider the dismissal of a citizen complaint.

items.item: Police deputy chief hiring process listening session
items.why: Police department employees will hold a listening session with the commission in closed session regarding the deputy chief hiring process.

preview.overview: The Police & Fire Commission will hear updates from both departments and hold closed sessions to interview police officer candidates, consider a fire lieutenant promotion candidate, and discuss a police deputy chief hiring process.
The school board is scheduled to meet in closed session to discuss contract matters. No public business appears on this agenda.

items.item: 2026 budget modification for year-end projections
items.why: The Finance Committee is asking the council to approve various budget adjustments based on how the year ended.

items.item: Salary structure revision for general city employees
items.why: The Finance Committee and Human Resources Committee are asking the council to revise how general employees' salaries are structured.

items.item: Special assessments for 2027 street construction projects
items.why: The Infrastructure & Facilities Committee is asking the council to levy special assessments (charges to property owners) to pay for street work in 2027.

items.item: Deed restrictions and non-conforming uses at 1300 Cleveland Avenue
items.why: The Economic Development Committee is asking the council to approve deed restrictions and clarify existing non-conforming uses on city-owned property.

items.item: Driveway and concrete approach exceptions for Kolbe & Kolbe Millwork
items.why: The Infrastructure & Facilities Committee is asking the council to approve oversized driveways and waive a concrete approach requirement at three nearby addresses on South 11th Avenue.

items.item: District 9 aldermanic vacancy
items.why: The Common Council is addressing how to fill an empty aldermanic seat in District 9.

preview.overview: The Common Council will vote on the 2026 budget modification and several resolutions affecting city property and employee pay. The council will also meet in closed session to discuss litigation strategy.

items.item: Public hearing and vote on 2027 budget
items.why: The council will hear public comment on the proposed 2027 budget and then vote on Resolution No. 2026-08 to adopt it and set the tax levy.

items.item: Building permit applications
items.why: The council will discuss and vote on pending building permit applications.

items.item: City employee holiday gift certificates
items.why: The council will discuss and decide whether to approve holiday gift certificates for city employees.

items.item: Police labor agreement modification
items.why: The council will discuss and vote on changes to the labor agreement with the Mosinee Professional Police Association that runs through December 31, 2026.

preview.overview: The City of Mosinee is scheduled to hold a public hearing on its 2027 budget and vote to approve it. The council will also decide on building permits, employee gifts, and a police labor agreement modification.

items.item: Recommendation for 2026 demolition of 207 North 1st Avenue
items.why: The board will make a recommendation on whether to demolish the building at 207 North 1st Avenue, with bids already opened.

items.item: Pay estimates for Crocker Street and Cherry Street lift stations
items.why: The board will approve a second payment to Haas Sons, Inc. for Crocker Street Lift Station Replacement and a final payment to Integrity Grading & Excavating, Inc. for Cherry Street Lift Station Replacement.

items.item: Pay estimates for downtown sidewalk and asphalt paving projects
items.why: The board will approve a first payment to Pember Companies, Inc. for the 2026 Downtown Sidewalk Improvement Project and a sixth payment plus final payment to RC Pavers, LLC for the 2026 Asphalt Paving Project A.

preview.overview: The Board of Public Works is scheduled to decide on demolishing a downtown building and approve payments for several ongoing street and utility projects around the city.

items.item: Aquatic Center Repairs update
items.why: Director Osterbrink will report on ongoing leak detection and equipment replacement work by Neuman Pools, including $12,000 for leak detection and $128,000 for new motors, pumps, and valves.

items.item: Farmers Market End of Season Survey results discussion
items.why: The committee will review feedback from 129 survey respondents about the market at Kennedy Park, covering parking, traffic flow, shade, and other visitor experiences.

items.item: Kennedy Park Master Plan update
items.why: The committee will discuss updates to the master plan, including whether to keep the Farmers Market at its current location and plans by youth hockey for the northwest corner of the park.

preview.overview: The Parks and Recreation Committee will hear updates on pool repairs costing $140,000 and review survey feedback from 129 Farmers Market visitors about their Kennedy Park experience. The committee may also discuss and act on results from the market survey and updates to the Kennedy Park Master Plan.

items.item: Animal impoundment services agreement with Humane Society
items.why: The committee will vote to approve a contract with the Humane Society of Marathon County for the city to use their animal impoundment services.

items.item: Five other service and equipment purchase agreements
items.why: The committee will vote to approve agreements for mapping software (Esri), county production services, cemetery operations, and fire department cardiac monitors and ventilators.

items.item: Budget change and lift purchase for Athletic Park
items.why: The committee will vote to approve a budget modification and sole source request to buy an outdoor vertical platform lift for Athletic Park.

items.item: Update on county pet license fee changes for 2027
items.why: City staff will update the committee on how Marathon County plans to change pet license fees starting in 2027.

preview.overview: The Finance Committee is scheduled to vote on six agreements and contracts for city services. These include animal impounding, mapping software, cemetery operations, and fire department equipment purchases.

items.item: Bikeshare program ridership data and spring promotion
items.why: The committee will review how many people are using the city's bikeshare program and plans for promoting it in spring.

items.item: Community Sustainability Survey results review
items.why: The committee will review results from a survey about community sustainability preferences.

items.item: MPO Bike/Ped Subcommittee update and bike counter data
items.why: The committee will get an update from the regional transportation planning group and hear bike counter data.

items.item: Adolph Street and River Edge Parkway pavement conditions
items.why: The committee will receive an update on the condition of pavement on these streets used by cyclists and pedestrians.

items.item: Police Department attendance and enabling language update
items.why: The committee will get an update on police involvement with the committee and related rules.

items.item: RRFB Thomas Street and River Edge Parkway
items.why: The committee will receive an update on a rectangular rapid flashing beacon (RRFB), a pedestrian safety signal, at this location.

preview.overview: The Bicycle & Pedestrian Advisory Committee will discuss Wausau's bikeshare program, review survey results about community sustainability, and get updates on bike and pedestrian infrastructure projects around the city.
